entry.title: Hovius v Speno Rail Maintenance Australia Pty Ltd [2026] NSWSC 1152
entry.content:
Mr Hovius sought judicial review of a Personal Injury Commission Medical Appeal Panel decision assessing his permanent impairment at 18% after workplace knee/hip injuries and scarring. The Supreme Court found the Appeal Panel failed to assess impairment in accordance with the workers compensation guidelines, failed to address all appeal grounds including pain and hip, and failed to give adequate reasons. The Court held he was entitled to the relief sought, including an extension of time.

Key holding: The workers compensation guidelines have delegated legislative force, and an Appeal Panel’s failure to assess permanent impairment in accordance with them can amount to a constructive failure to exercise jurisdiction.

Those guidelines have the force or effect of delegated legislation and failure to carry out an assessment in accordance with them may constitute a constructive failure to exercise jurisdiction.

Supreme Court of New South Wales, 12 Oct 2026, [2026] NSWSC 1152

entry.title: Frazer v State of Queensland [2026] QSC 82 (22 April 2026)
entry.content:
Ms Frazer, an experienced teacher, sued the State of Queensland after suffering PTSD following an incident where an aggrieved parent attended the school looking to confront her. The State admitted it owed a non-delegable duty of care to Ms Frazer, but disputed breach. The court found no breach and entered judgment for the defendant.

Key holding: A policy authorising physical force to remove an abusive or threatening person does not require force in every circumstance; reasonableness depends on the unfolding situation.

It seems to me that the authorisation in Chief Executive Guideline No 1 of 2012 to take all reasonable steps including physical force to eject an abusive, threatening or disorderly person does not, could not and should not demand in all circumstances that physical force be used to eject an abusive, threatening or disorderly person.

Supreme Court of Queensland, 22 Apr 2026, [2026] QSC 82

entry.title: Gong v AWI Steel Pty Limited [2026] NSWSC 331 (9 April 2026)
entry.content:
Mr Gong, a boilermaker/welder contracted through Gong Engineering to work at AWI Steel's factory, suffered serious injuries when a heavy metal plate he was attempting to manually flip slipped and fell on him. The court found that AWI breached its duty of care to Mr Gong by failing to provide a safe system of work for Korean-speaking contractors, including proper induction and supervision, and that AWI bears primary responsibility for the accident, though Mr Gong's own contributory negligence reduces his recoverable damages.

Supreme Court of New South Wales, 9 Apr 2026, [2026] NSWSC 331

entry.title: Kwiatkowski v Plum Pictures Limited (No 3) [2026] NSWSC 288 (31 March 2026)
entry.content:
A personal injury plaintiff (injured on a TV shoot in 2016) sought to adjourn proceedings to comply with pre-litigation requirements under the WIM Act after belatedly seeking to add a workers compensation damages claim in the alternative. The defendant sought dismissal for non-compliance with those requirements. Campbell J refused dismissal but stayed the proceedings, giving the plaintiff time to comply while retaining judicial oversight.

Supreme Court of New South Wales, 31 Mar 2026, [2026] NSWSC 288

entry.title: Insurance Australia Limited t/as NRMA Insurance v Kwarteng [2026] NSWSC 225 (24 March 2026)
entry.content:
NRMA Insurance sought judicial review of a PIC Review Panel decision that revoked a 5% whole person impairment assessment and substituted a 12% assessment for a motor accident claimant, thereby crossing the 10% threshold for non-economic loss damages under the MAI Act. The Supreme Court dismissed the summons on all three grounds, finding the Review Panel properly exercised its collective judgment and adequately exposed its reasoning.

Supreme Court of New South Wales, 24 Mar 2026, [2026] NSWSC 225

entry.title: O'Driscoll v Encore Aviation Pty Ltd (No 2) [2026] NSWSC 205 (16 March 2026)
entry.content:
This is a costs decision following a helicopter crash personal injury and corporate loss trial. The court considered whether indemnity costs should follow an unaccepted offer of compromise under UCPR r 42.15, and whether costs should be reduced for a partially successful corporate plaintiff. The first plaintiff recovered only $55,250 against a $200,000 offer; the second plaintiff's judgment was increased to $627,732.41 but with costs limited to 80%.

Supreme Court of New South Wales, 16 Mar 2026, [2026] NSWSC 205

entry.title: Bath v Allianz Australia Insurance Limited [2026] NSWSC 165 (9 March 2026)
entry.content:
The plaintiff was injured when he fell from his mobility scooter on a Sydney Light Rail vehicle. A Personal Injury Commission review panel assessed his whole person impairment (WPI) at only 5%, below the 10% threshold for non-economic loss damages, after finding his shoulder injuries were not caused by the accident. The Supreme Court set aside the panel's decision for jurisdictional error in treating the absence of contemporaneous medical documentation as decisive of causation.

Supreme Court of New South Wales, 9 Mar 2026, [2026] NSWSC 165

entry.title: Anderson v Claytons Towing Service Pty Ltd & Ors [2026] QSC 26 (5 March 2026)
entry.content:
A tow truck driver was seriously injured when a bus rolled forward off wooden blocks while he was underneath attaching towing equipment. The bus owner had released the handbrake despite being explicitly told not to. The court found the employer liable for a defective system of work and the bus owner liable for releasing the handbrake, with the third-party CTP insurer also liable under the Motor Accident Insurance Act 1994 (Qld).

Supreme Court of Queensland, 5 Mar 2026, [2026] QSC 26

entry.title: Hussain Al-Azam v Ahmed Khagany [2026] NSWDC 29 (4 March 2026)
entry.content:
Default judgment damages assessment in a personal injury claim arising from a fall through a Colorbond roof. The plaintiff, a 62-year-old Iraqi-born refugee with pre-existing PTSD, suffered a fractured left femur, pubic ramus fracture, bilateral shoulder injuries, and aggravation of psychiatric conditions when a granny flat roof collapsed beneath him. The defendant, who was holding the ladder, never appeared, and Cole DCJ assessed damages at $1,005,598.

District Court of New South Wales, 4 Mar 2026, [2026] NSWDC 29

entry.title: Ypermachou v PMK Pty Ltd [2026] NSWSC 149 (4 March 2026)
entry.content:
A self-represented plaintiff sought judicial review in the NSW Supreme Court of a Personal Injury Commission Appeal Panel decision that dismissed his appeal against medical assessment certificates assessing his permanent impairment from a 1995 workplace injury. The Court dismissed the summons, finding no reviewable error in the Appeal Panel's reasons.

Supreme Court of New South Wales, 4 Mar 2026, [2026] NSWSC 149

entry.title: Ardis-Phasey v Neal & Anor [2026] QDC 25 (27 February 2026)
entry.content:
A 20-year-old plaintiff claimed damages for a persistent lower back injury sustained in a motor vehicle accident at age 14. Liability was admitted; the trial concerned quantum only. The Court awarded $182,800 in total damages, including $15,300 for general damages (ISV 9) and a significant component for future economic loss, with indemnity costs from the date of an unaccepted offer.

District Court of Queensland, 27 Feb 2026, [2026] QDC 25

entry.title: Cheng v Jones Lang Lasalle (NSW) Pty Ltd [2026] NSWDC 12 (23 February 2026)
entry.content:
Occupiers' liability claim arising from a trip-and-fall at Eastgate Shopping Centre, Bondi Junction. The plaintiff tripped on a services cover (electrical access panel) in the common area near a pop-up store. The District Court found the defendant occupier negligent and awarded $72,240 after a 25% reduction for contributory negligence.

District Court of New South Wales, 23 Feb 2026, [2026] NSWDC 12

entry.title: Greenall v Amaca Pty Ltd [2026] QSC 16 (19 February 2026)
entry.content:
Estate claim for damages arising from mesothelioma caused by occupational asbestos exposure during roofing work with James Hardie products in Queensland in 1972. Liability was admitted; the sole contest was quantum of general damages, with the plaintiff claiming $800,000 and the defendant submitting $200,000. Smith J awarded judgment for $157,598.18.

Supreme Court of Queensland, 19 Feb 2026, [2026] QSC 16
